headline: Avalanche’s Logan O’Connor expected to make season debut against Lightning
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Avalanche forward Logan O'Connor is expected to make his season debut against the Lightning. He had been dealing with a lower-body injury and also took time away from the team after his father's passing.

His return lands on a Colorado team that has been good at creating chances. So far this season, COL has taken 58.5% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality that tells you who generated the better chances), and 55% at five-on-five, where most of the game is played. The Avalanche are 5-2-1, and their results have run well ahead of those chances: they have scored 6.9 more goals than expected. That kind of gap tends to shrink, so a healthy lineup matters for keeping the process strong rather than leaning on finishing luck. The matchup is a real test, since TBL is almost identical at 59% of the expected goals overall and 59% at five-on-five. The Lightning, 6-2-0, have been the opposite story, scoring 4.9 fewer goals than expected, which suggests their record understates how well they have played. Colorado's penalty kill (0.32 expected goals allowed per game) also grades better than Tampa Bay's (0.53).
